clue.text: O'Neill's daughter of singer / songwriter / actor, it's said

definitions.text: O'Neill's daughter of singer / songwriter / actor, it's said

parts.words: O'Neill's daughter of singer / songwriter / actor, it's said
parts.note: the title heroine of Eugene O'Neill's play is the daughter of the sailor Chris Christopherson, a name that sounds like that of the singer, songwriter and actor Kris Kristofferson

explanation.surface: A gossip item about which celebrity performer a playwright's heroine is descended from.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill's 1921 play takes its title from its heroine, a sailor's daughter.

clue.text: The school featuring appearances by Matthew Arnold and T. H. Huxley?

definitions.text: The school featuring appearances by Matthew Arnold and T. H. Huxley?

parts.words: The school featuring appearances by Matthew Arnold and T. H. Huxley?
parts.note: the Victorian sage and the scientist were both public figures of learned institutions, and the word also names Plato's school of philosophy in Athens

explanation.surface: A prospectus boasting of two famous Victorian guest lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's school of philosophy took its name from the grove of Akademos, and any learned society or college can bear the name.

clue.text: Novelist from Sinai. Paul Bowles, perhaps?

definitions.text: Novelist

indicators.note: the novelist's name is taken out of the run of letters across the two words, ignoring the full stop

explanation.surface: A question whether an American writer of desert fiction might have come out of Sinai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paul Bowles, perhaps?' adds a second example of a novelist: Bowles wrote of North Africa, as V. S. Naipaul wrote of the developing world.
explanation.definitionFit: V. S. Naipaul was a Trinidad-born Nobel-winning writer of fiction such as A House for Mr Biswas.

clue.text: Dim Capone destroys summaries of larger works

definitions.text: summaries of larger works

indicators.note: to destroy is to wreck, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A slow-witted gangster tears up his reading digests.
explanation.definitionFit: A compendium is a concise digest of a fuller treatise; the Latin plural is used here.

clue.text: To turn back to zero is confusing for Steer

definitions.text: To turn back to zero

indicators.note: something confusing is jumbled, so the letters of the word Steer are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone at a wheel finds it bewildering to wind a dial back to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a counter or device again to its starting value is what a reset does.

clue.text: Poet might take on as a novelist

definitions.text: Poet might take on as a novelist

parts.words: Poet might take on as a novelist
parts.note: the surname of the American poet Wallace, with the two letters of the word on added at its end, becomes the surname of the Scottish novelist Robert Louis

explanation.surface: A poet ponders switching careers to writing fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace Stevens was the American poet of Harmonium; adding ON turns his surname into that of the author of Treasure Island.

clue.text: Villains of every stripe have difficulty keeping up with this particular Jones

definitions.text: Villains of every stripe have difficulty keeping up with this particular Jones

parts.words: Villains of every stripe have difficulty keeping up with this particular Jones
parts.note: the film archaeologist with the whip and fedora, first name taken from a US state, outruns all manner of villains

explanation.surface: A remark on keeping up with the Joneses, as if the neighbours were criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana Jones is the adventuring archaeologist of the Spielberg film series.

clue.text: Not a Spring baby, we hear, this admirer of Miss Miller

definitions.text: this admirer of Miss Miller

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the solver's spoken words, not their spelling, give the name

parts.note: someone born in the cold season rather than spring is winter-born

explanation.surface: A gossip notes that Daisy Miller's suitor had a birthday in the colder months.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Miller is Henry James's novella; Frederick Winterbourne is the young American who admires her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Henry James's Daisy Miller, Winterbourne is the expatriate who is drawn to the heroine.

clue.text: Wartime distraction for Amy Lowell

definitions.text: Wartime distraction for Amy Lowell

parts.note: the American poet championed and edited anthologies of a poetic movement of sharp clear pictures in 1915 to 1917, during the First World War

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a poet kept herself busy while war raged.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagism was the early-twentieth-century movement of precise visual poetry that Amy Lowell promoted, launched by Pound.

clue.text: He had a shallow cousin and a simple servant

definitions.text: He had a shallow cousin and a simple servant

parts.words: He had a shallow cousin and a simple servant
parts.note: in The Merry Wives of Windsor a thin young suitor is the cousin of Justice Shallow and the master of the servant Simple

explanation.surface: An unflattering description of a man's superficial relative and dim helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Slender is Shakespeare's foolish suitor to Anne Page in The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Anti-novelist exhibited jealousy in 1957

definitions.text: Anti-novelist exhibited jealousy in 1957

parts.note: the French nouveau roman writer published La Jalousie in 1957, so he put Jealousy on show

explanation.surface: A writer opposed to novels lost his temper with envy one year.
explanation.definitionFit: Alain Robbe-Grillet led the French nouveau roman, often called the anti-novel, and wrote La Jalousie.

clue.text: "sex-change priest in mercy dash to Palace" (Magnus Linklater)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "sex-change priest in mercy dash to Palace" (Magnus Linklater): no wordplay or definition for the answer can be found, and a search of the quotation gave nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: "sex-change priest in mercy dash to Palace" (Magnus Linklater)

clue.text: No absolute is going to make the lion lie with it unless it is inside, Lawrence thought

definitions.text: No absolute is going to make the lion lie with it unless it is inside, Lawrence thought

parts.words: No absolute is going to make the lion lie with it unless it is inside, Lawrence thought
parts.note: D. H. Lawrence's aphorism says the beast of prey will only lie down with its gentle companion once it has eaten it, the young sheep of Isaiah's prophecy

explanation.surface: A quotation from D. H. Lawrence on the impossibility of peace between predator and prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's line reworks the biblical image of the lion lying down with the young sheep.

clue.text: Malraux's novel route ()

definitions.text: Malraux's novel route ()

parts.note: André Malraux's novel La Voie ... names a regal way, the adjective filling the empty brackets

explanation.surface: A reference to the road travelled in a French novel, with a word left blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Malraux's La Voie royale translates as The Royal Way, so the missing word is the regal adjective.

clue.text: One direction of rake's progress in the theatre

definitions.text: One direction of rake's progress in the theatre

parts.words: One direction of rake's progress in the theatre
parts.note: a stage's rake is its slope, and moving towards the audience goes down that slope

explanation.surface: A Hogarth-style libertine's career told as a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: On a raked stage the front, nearest the audience, is lower, hence the term for moving toward it.

clue.text: Condition of Maid Marian at end of the story

definitions.text: Condition of Maid Marian at end of the story

parts.words: Condition of Maid Marian at end of the story
parts.note: when the outlaw of Sherwood dies at the close of the legend, his sweetheart is left bereaved

explanation.surface: A question about the outlaw's sweetheart's state when the tale ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a woman whose husband has died is her state; the word splits as Widow Hood, Robin's widow.

clue.text: Like a stage whisper by Ustinov?

definitions.text: Like a stage whisper by Ustinov?

parts.words: Like a stage whisper by Ustinov?
parts.note: a stage whisper is meant to be caught by others, and Peter Ustinov wrote a 1981 play with that very title

explanation.surface: A remark about an actor-playwright's theatrically loud whisper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage whisper is designed to be heard by the audience, and Ustinov's play bears the same title.

clue.text: Give hot version of book size

definitions.text: book size

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply a spicy edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo, written 8vo and spoken in full, is a book format of sheets folded into eight leaves.

clue.text: Popular scientist introduces friend of Falstaff with nationality of Horatio

definitions.text: Popular scientist

parts.note: Prince Hal is Falstaff's drinking companion in Henry IV
Horatio, Hamlet's friend, is taken here as a Dane

explanation.surface: A science writer is introduced to Shakespearean company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' just joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. S. Haldane was a geneticist and widely read writer of science for general readers.

clue.text: Imply no Dante work

definitions.text: Imply

indicators.note: the word no is itself the pair of letters dropped, and it signals that they are absent

parts.note: the Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: Suggest that something was not written by the Florentine poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' tells you to take the letters NO off the end of INFERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: The two verbs are often confused, and loosely the one is used for hinting or suggesting.

clue.text: Hardly a hero for Colin Wilson, Richard Wright, or Camus

definitions.text: Hardly a hero for Colin Wilson, Richard Wright, or Camus

parts.words: Hardly a hero for Colin Wilson, Richard Wright, or Camus
parts.note: each of these writers produced a book called The Outsider, so their figure is the opposite of someone in the know

explanation.surface: An observation about the kind of protagonist three writers would not choose.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to the inner circle, the opposite of the alienated figure in those three books.

clue.text: These are the arks…/ That thy name against old age" (Samuel Daniel)

definitions.text: These are the arks…/ That thy name against old age" (Samuel Daniel)

parts.words: These are the arks…/ That thy name against old age" (Samuel Daniel)
parts.note: the missing verb in Daniel's sonnet line means strengthen or defend

explanation.surface: A quotation from Samuel Daniel's sonnets with its verb left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen or make secure against attack is what the poems do for the beloved's name.

clue.text: Star Punic War hero

definitions.text: Star
definitions.meaning: the brightest star in the constellation Leo

definitions.text: Punic War hero
definitions.meaning: Marcus Atilius ..., Roman consul captured by Carthage in the First Punic War

explanation.surface: A celebrity who fought in Rome's wars with Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a bright point of light in Leo and to a legendary Roman consul famed for keeping his word to Carthage.

clue.text: Get going start some early Thomas Tallis oratorios

definitions.text: Get going

indicators.note: only some of the letters, the opening one of each word, are used here

explanation.surface: A choir is urged to begin some early English sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to the first letters of start, early, Thomas, Tallis, oratorios.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is an idiom for beginning work in earnest.

clue.text: Part of Shelley's circle was Trelawney a spendthrift

definitions.text: a spendthrift

indicators.note: only a portion of the letters running across the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Gossip that one of Shelley's friends was a squanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Trelawny was a friend of Shelley and Byron; the clue spells him Trelawney.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a good-for-nothing who squanders money.

clue.text: "…out of thee one spark of evil / That might annoy my finger?" (Henry V)

definitions.text: "…out of thee one spark of evil / That might annoy my finger?" (Henry V)

parts.words: "…out of thee one spark of evil / That might annoy my finger?" (Henry V)
parts.note: the king asks whether anyone could draw or pull out a single spark of evil from the traitor, the verb missing before the quotation

explanation.surface: A line from Henry V about a traitor's hidden malice, its verb left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out is the meaning of the missing verb in the king's speech.

clue.text: One of those purveying a tale by Arnold Bennett, perhaps?

definitions.text: One of those purveying a tale by Arnold Bennett, perhaps?

parts.words: One of those purveying a tale by Arnold Bennett, perhaps?
parts.note: Bennett's novel is The Old Wives' Tale, and such a tale is folk superstition passed on by elderly women

explanation.surface: Wondering who tells a Bennett story aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly women are proverbially the tellers of superstitious tales, as in Bennett's title.

clue.text: Not another Hardy sergeant for Yeats?

definitions.text: Not another Hardy sergeant for Yeats?

parts.words: Not another Hardy sergeant for Yeats?
parts.note: Yeats wrote a poem lamenting that there was not a further city to burn, and Hardy's Sergeant Francis Troy of Far from the Madding Crowd shares that city's name

explanation.surface: Yeats is spared a second dashing soldier from Hardy's Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats's poem about Maud Gonne asks what other city she could have burned, Helen-like, since none remained.
